findings.consequence: If a pallet jams at the entry photo-eye, the conveyor motor will continue running indefinitely against the blocked pallet instead of tripping, which could lead to mechanical damage or excessive wear.
findings.evidence: According to the narrative (§3) and the cause-and-effect matrix (CE-ST10-03), if the entry photo-eye PE-1002 (X11) stays blocked for more than 5.0 s while the conveyor runs, the conveyor must stop and a jam alarm must be raised. The lint block shows X11 is unused. While M190 (the jam alarm) is reset in R2 and used to drop the motor in R3, the logic to actually set M190 is entirely missing.
findings.proposed_fix:
Add the missing jam detection logic before R3 to monitor the photo-eye and set the jam flag. For example:
LD X11
AND Y10
OUT T10 K50
LD T10
SET M190
findings.title: Missing Conveyor Jam Detection Logic

data.summary: The ST10 conveyor program correctly implements the E-stop, motor overload interlocking, and the automated stopper release sequence. However, the logic for the pallet jam detection (PE-1002 / X11) has been omitted. Adding the 5.0-second timer and latch for the jam alarm (M190) will bring the program into compliance with the control narrative and cause-and-effect matrix.
